text:
infra-bot: INCIDENT: Multiple driver resets (Xid 86/31) observed on node serve-prod-gpu-3. Paging oncall. Tags: #gpu #driver #xid :rotating_light:

sachin: saw the alert, taking a look. hopping into node console now.

ellen: noticed spikes in container restarts ~ 10:12 UTC, correlates with high mem usage on that host.

maria: adding logs here — dmesg shows repeated: 
```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 86, PID=4623, GPU has fallen off the bus
NVRM: GPU ec0: ECC error on memory controller
```

sachin: thanks — also seeing OOM kills in kube events for model-worker pods on that node. stack traces look like allocation failures during kv-cache growth.

ellen: quick probe: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,fb_memory_usage --format=csv` shows erratic fb usage jumps before resets.

maria: running `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=spec.nodeName=serve-prod-gpu-3` — 6 pods restarted in last 8m, most are model-worker-v2.

tim: any customer-facing errors yet? pg-monitor shows error-rate increase (500s) on /v1/generate for region us-west-2 between 10:11-10:18. Some retries kicked in.

oncall-next: I'm oncall-next, standing by to take handoff in 15.

sachin: mitigation plan I'm doing now: 1) cordon node serve-prod-gpu-3 2) drain non-critical pods (batch jobs) 3) move model-worker pods to fallback pool with quantized model variant 4) monitor for further Xid.

ellen: executing cordon/drain: 
```
kubectl cordon serve-prod-gpu-3
kubectl drain serve-prod-gpu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=critical-proxy' --grace-period=30
```

maria: migrating heavy workers to serve-prod-gpu-1 and serve-prod-gpu-2, applied affinity tolerations for fallback. Rolling until node drain completes.

deploy-bot: INFO: Canary fallback route activated: /v1/generate -> model-quantized-256 (50% for affected hosts).

tim: customer impact summary so far: about ~2% of requests in US-WEST had 500s, mainly long-sequence generation jobs. No major outage but increased latency and a few failed batches. Customer team notified for top 5 heavy tenants.

sachin: looking at NIC/PCI errors — PCI link flaps not obvious. ECC counts non-zero. Could be a failing DIMM on the GPU or driver regression.

ellen: quick kernel/driver version check: nvidia-driver 525.85.05, kernel 5.15.0-1127. No recent deploys to that node. hardware vendor has a firmware update but not yet applied.

maria: suggestion: keep node cordoned, continue drain. If driver resets persist after pod migration, we should power-cycle node and check nvram logs and vendor hw tests.

sachin: agreed. also lowering batch size and request concurrency for other nodes to absorb load. will open a short incident doc.

oncall-next: I'll take the post-drain monitoring (10m intervals) and handle vendor escalation if the reboot doesn't clear Xid. handoff at 10:30 UTC.

tim: timeline note for incident doc: 10:11 alert -> 10:14 cordon start -> 10:18 drain started -> 10:24 fallback route applied -> 10:28 drain complete (node reserved).

maria: logs attached in internal storage: /mnt/logs/incidents/1798501234/gpu3_dmesg.log and `kubectl describe pod` snippets.

sachin: manual memory blacklist applied to model-worker (reduced kv-cache target). command: 
```
kubectl set env deployment/model-worker KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=536870912
```

ellen: monitoring metrics: ECC corrected errors count increased by 12 in last 30m. That's higher than expected baseline.

deploy-bot: ALERT: Route fallback reduced error-rate to baseline after 3m.

tim: customer comms draft: "We observed driver resets affecting a subset of GPU hosts causing intermittent failures and latency increases between 10:11-10:28 UTC. We routed traffic to fallback model variants and drained affected host. No persistent data loss; full mitigation in progress. We'll update if node reboots or vendor confirms hardware issue." Open to edits.

sachin: plan next: keep node cordoned overnight, schedule maintenance window to reboot and run vendor hardware diagnostics. If reboot clears, uncordon and monitor for 24h. If not, RMA the GPU/host.

oncall-next: taking handoff now. I'm @oncall-next. I'll watch health checks and vendor queue. Please ping me for escalation. :thumbsup:

maria: adding postmortem owner tag: @sachin to draft once incident quiet.

ellen: final check — any remaining restarts? kube events for serve-prod-gpu-3 show none after 10:28. good.

sachin: closing thread for active mitigation. if we see Xid recurrence reopen and call for immediate reboot. thanks team. :raised_hands:
